_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Belgium covering Gallia Belgica (Caesar 'bravest of all Gauls'), Frankish kingdoms, Burgundian Netherlands, Habsburg rule, Spanish Netherlands, Austrian Netherlands, French Revolution annexation, Congress of Vienna 1815 (United Kingdom of Netherlands), Belgian Revolution 1830, Leopold I, Congo Free State (Leopold II, 1885-1908, genocide ~10M killed), WWI Western Front (Ypres, Flanders Fields, Belgian neutrality violated), WWII German occupation, EU/NATO headquarters (Brussels), linguistic divide (Flemish-Walloon), and federal devolution.

religion.note: Catholic historically dominant (Counter-Reformation, Belgian identity); declining practice; Muslim community (Moroccan/Turkish immigration, Brussels ~25% Muslim); secularisation rapid; Jewish community (Antwerp diamond trade, Orthodox Jews); pillarisation (Catholic/Liberal/Socialist 'pillars')

ethnic_groups.name: Flemish (Dutch-speaking)
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern Flanders; Dutch dialect; economically dominant today; cultural connection to Netherlands; Flemish nationalism/independence movement; historically subordinated to French-speaking elite

ethnic_groups.name: Walloon (French-speaking)
ethnic_groups.notes: Southern Wallonia; French-speaking; historically dominant (industry, elite); post-industrial decline; Walloon identity

ethnic_groups.name: Brussels (bilingual)
ethnic_groups.notes: Capital region; officially bilingual (French dominant ~85%); multicultural; EU quarter cosmopolitan; Flemish enclave geographically

ethnic_groups.name: German-speaking
ethnic_groups.notes: Eastern cantons (Eupen-Malmedy); awarded to Belgium after WWI; ~77,000; own community government

ethnic_groups.name: Other/foreign origin
ethnic_groups.notes: Moroccan (~500k), Turkish, Italian (coal miners), Congolese, Polish, Romanian; 15%+ foreign-born; Brussels most cosmopolitan EU city

country_profile.notes_unique: EU headquarters (Brussels, European Commission/Council/Parliament, 'capital of Europe'); NATO HQ; Belgian Congo (Leopold II's personal colony 1885-1908, rubber terror, ~10M killed/maimed, 'heart of darkness', hands cut off); WWI Western Front (German invasion August 1914, 'brave little Belgium', Ypres/Passchendaele, Flanders Fields poppy poem, 500,000+ died on Belgian soil); linguistic divide (Dutch/French, 'language border' since 1962); 6 governments (federal + 3 regions + 3 communities); 541 days without government (2010-11, world record); chocolate (pralines inventor), beer (UNESCO, 1,500+ varieties), waffles, frites; Tintin (Hergé); Art Nouveau (Horta); Surrealism (Magritte); Battle of Waterloo 1815; Atomium

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global. 'rank' = 1 is best/largest.

910.name: Gallia Belgica & the Roman Era
910.description: Caesar's conquest of the Belgae—whom he called the bravest of the Gauls—created the province of Gallia Belgica. Roman roads, villas, and the city of Tongeren (Atuatuca Tungrorum) shaped the region's early urbanisation.

sub_clusters.name: Belgae Tribes & Caesar's Conquest
sub_clusters.description: Julius Caesar's campaigns against the Nervii, Eburones (Ambiorix's revolt), and other Belgic tribes, and the subsequent establishment of Gallia Belgica.
key_events: Caesar defeats the Nervii at the Battle of the Sabis (57 BCE)
Ambiorix's revolt and destruction of a Roman legion (54 BCE)

sub_clusters.name: Roman Belgica & Early Urbanism
sub_clusters.description: Development of Tongeren as the provincial capital, Roman road networks, villa estates, and the gradual Christianisation and Frankish settlement in late antiquity.

920.name: Frankish Kingdoms & Carolingian Heartland
920.description: The Low Countries formed the core of the Frankish realms. Clovis's conversion, the Carolingian rise from Liège and Aachen, and the Treaty of Verdun's division profoundly shaped Belgian identity.

sub_clusters.name: Merovingian Frankish Heartland
sub_clusters.description: Clovis and the Merovingian dynasty ruling from the Low Countries, the Christianisation of Flanders, and the rise of the Carolingian mayors of the palace.

sub_clusters.name: Carolingian Empire & Treaty of Verdun
sub_clusters.description: Charlemagne's empire centred near Aachen/Liège, and the Treaty of Verdun (843) dividing the region between Lotharingia and West Francia, setting the linguistic divide.
key_events: Treaty of Verdun divides the Carolingian Empire (843)

920.name: Medieval Flanders & the Cloth Trade
920.description: The County of Flanders became one of Europe's wealthiest regions through its cloth industry. Cities like Bruges, Ghent, and Ypres rivalled Italian city-states in commercial sophistication.

sub_clusters.name: Flemish Cloth Cities
sub_clusters.description: The rise of Bruges, Ghent, and Ypres as major textile centres, guild power, and the growing tensions between urban craftsmen, counts, and the French crown.

sub_clusters.name: Battle of the Golden Spurs & Aftermath
sub_clusters.description: The Flemish militia's stunning victory over French knights at Kortrijk (1302), a landmark in urban and national identity, and the subsequent turbulent century of revolts.
key_events: Battle of the Golden Spurs at Kortrijk (1302)

930.name: Burgundian & Habsburg Netherlands
930.description: Under Burgundian dukes the Low Countries were unified into a prosperous cultural bloc. Habsburg inheritance brought the region into Charles V's world empire, followed by the traumatic Dutch Revolt that split north from south.

sub_clusters.name: Burgundian Golden Age
sub_clusters.description: The Burgundian dukes' unification of the Low Countries, the court culture of Philip the Good, patronage of Jan van Eyck and Flemish Primitives, and Charles the Bold's ambitions.

sub_clusters.name: Habsburg Rule & the Dutch Revolt
sub_clusters.description: Mary of Burgundy's marriage to Maximilian I, Charles V's consolidation, Philip II's religious persecution, the Iconoclast Fury, the Duke of Alba's Council of Troubles, and the split between rebellious north and loyalist south.
key_events: Iconoclastic Fury sweeps the Low Countries (1566)
Union of Arras – southern provinces remain under Spain (1579)

930.name: Spanish Netherlands
930.description: The southern Low Countries under Spanish Habsburg rule experienced the splendour of Rubens's Antwerp alongside devastating warfare, culminating in transfer to Austrian Habsburg control.

sub_clusters.name: Archducal Period & Rubens' Antwerp
sub_clusters.description: The reign of Archdukes Albert and Isabella, the Twelve Years' Truce, Rubens's artistic dominance, and the final recognition of Dutch independence at Westphalia.

sub_clusters.name: Battlefield of Europe
sub_clusters.description: Louis XIV's wars repeatedly devastated the Spanish Netherlands, culminating in the War of the Spanish Succession and the transfer to Austrian Habsburg control at Utrecht (1713).

940.name: Austrian Netherlands & Belgian Revolution
940.description: Austrian rule, brief French annexation, forced merger with the Netherlands, and the Belgian Revolution of 1830 that created an independent Belgium with a liberal constitutional monarchy.

sub_clusters.name: Austrian Habsburg & French Revolutionary Period
sub_clusters.description: Austrian Habsburg governance, the Brabant Revolution (1789), French annexation and Napoleonic integration, and the Battle of Waterloo fought on Belgian soil.

sub_clusters.name: Belgian Revolution of 1830
sub_clusters.description: Forced union with the Netherlands under William I, growing Belgian discontent, the opera-night revolution of August 1830, and international recognition via the Treaty of London (1839).
key_events: Belgian Revolution begins at Brussels opera house (August 1830)
Treaty of London guarantees Belgian independence and neutrality (1839)

940.name: Leopold II & the Congo Free State
940.description: Leopold II's personal colonial venture in the Congo became one of history's most notorious regimes of exploitation, provoking an international humanitarian outcry that forced Belgium to annex the territory.

sub_clusters.name: Congo Free State & Rubber Terror
sub_clusters.description: Leopold II's ruthless extraction of rubber and ivory, forced labour, mutilations, the investigative work of E.D. Morel and Roger Casement, and the eventual transfer to Belgian state control.
key_events: Berlin Conference grants Leopold II personal control of the Congo (1885)

950.name: Belgium in World War I
950.description: Germany's violation of Belgian neutrality in 1914 brought Britain into the war and subjected Belgium to brutal occupation. Flanders Fields became synonymous with the horror of trench warfare.

sub_clusters.name: German Invasion & 'Rape of Belgium'
sub_clusters.description: Germany's invasion through Belgium, atrocities against civilians at Leuven and Dinant, the destruction of Leuven's university library, and King Albert I's resistance at the Yser.
key_events: German army burns Leuven's university library (August 1914)

sub_clusters.name: Flanders Fields & Trench Warfare
sub_clusters.description: The Ypres Salient, poison gas at Second Ypres, Passchendaele, and the enduring cultural legacy of John McCrae's 'In Flanders Fields'.

950.name: Belgium in World War II
950.description: The 18-day campaign, German occupation, collaboration and resistance, the Holocaust of Belgian Jews, the Battle of the Bulge in the Ardennes, and the divisive Royal Question over Leopold III.

sub_clusters.name: Occupation, Collaboration & Resistance
sub_clusters.description: Leopold III's controversial surrender, the Rexist and VNV collaboration movements, deportation of Belgian Jews from Mechelen transit camp, and active resistance networks.

sub_clusters.name: Liberation & the Royal Question
sub_clusters.description: Liberation by Allied forces, the Battle of the Bulge in the Ardennes (1944–45), and the Royal Question crisis over Leopold III's wartime conduct.
key_events: Battle of the Bulge fought in the Belgian Ardennes (Dec 1944 – Jan 1945)

960.name: EU/NATO Headquarters & European Identity
960.description: Belgium positioned itself as the institutional heart of Europe, hosting NATO headquarters and the European Commission, while navigating decolonisation of the Congo and domestic linguistic tensions.

sub_clusters.name: Capital of Europe
sub_clusters.description: Brussels as the seat of NATO (1967), the European Commission, and the Council of the EU, making Belgium the de facto capital of European integration.
key_events: Brussels becomes seat of the European Commission

sub_clusters.name: Congo Decolonisation
sub_clusters.description: The rushed independence of the Belgian Congo (1960), the Congo Crisis, Lumumba's assassination, and Belgium's troubled colonial legacy.

960.name: Linguistic Divide & Federal Belgium
960.description: Belgium's transformation from a unitary to a federal state driven by the Flemish-Walloon linguistic divide, including the splitting of the University of Leuven, repeated constitutional reforms, and prolonged government formation crises.

sub_clusters.name: Flemish-Walloon Conflict & Federalisation
sub_clusters.description: The linguistic frontier fixed in 1962, the splitting of the University of Leuven (1968), and successive state reforms creating Flanders, Wallonia, and Brussels-Capital regions.

sub_clusters.name: Modern Federal Belgium
sub_clusters.description: The fully federal state from 1993, the 2010–2011 record-breaking government formation crisis (541 days), far-right Vlaams Belang challenges, and Belgium's continued role as the EU's institutional heart.
